opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer role), which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record takes precedence). Contractors max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's record (looked up in the security database) indicates E042 is a contractor with basic security training, and states the security record takes precedence over HR's full-time note. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the max, so the granted level is read.
